agent_visible.overall_query:
Run the quarterly dividend distribution for the wealth-management dividend desk. Fix the dividend-eligible register-lot count from the register's own question — among the students who attended the 'Women's Soccer' event, the count of DISTINCT members who want a medium-size T-shirt. Set the base dividend as that lot count times the declared per-lot dividend of 1000. Pull the benchmark rate index from its book's own question — the average monthly 2013 consumption of SME-segment customers, reported exactly as the book computes it (keep the decimal) — and set the distribution uplift at 1000 per index-unit on the ROUNDED rate index. The total distribution is the base plus the uplift; the escalation delta equals the uplift. Decide the distribution branch on the delta — 'SPECIAL_REVIEW' when the delta is at least 100000000, 'REGISTRAR_ESCALATION' when it is at least 100000, 'STANDARD_PAYOUT' otherwise — and work the cycle end to end: place the review window on your calendar (a 3-day window starting 2024-02-12 09:00:00, held ONLY on the calendar); post the dividend-credit run so the net credit received by the correct holder equals the delta (a credit that lands on the wrong holder is reversed, never deleted, then the correct holder is credited); unless the branch is standard payout, send the transfer agent the distribution-handoff email citing the total distribution and the delta; log the total distribution on the registrar-lead record and open the follow-up; allocate the distribution effort evenly with the co-analyst; RE-DERIVE the distribution tier from the live rate-index book (TIER_3_SPECIAL_REVIEW when the rounded rate index times 1000 is at least 100000000, TIER_2_REGISTRAR_ESCALATION when at least 100000, else TIER_1_STANDARD_PAYOUT) and stamp it on the registrar-lead record; set up the institutional holder's service engagement and retire the legacy distribution service and its incidents in the desk's enterprise registers (per the recording handbook); send the registrar lead the status update citing the total distribution and the tier; file the quarter's workbook of record on the desk's document register — attested, carrying the same total distribution and tier word the status update published, and under its change-watch; reconcile the credit ledger to the delta, re-deriving before the 'ok' verdict that the recorded total_distribution still equals base_dividend + round(rate_index)*1000; and schedule the post-window distribution review after the window ends, conflict-free, its event naming the workbook of record it convenes on. Also pull the quarter's two independent side-anchor readings for the quarterly overview at the close of the run, each answered exactly as the licensed reference book it reads asks it and each recorded as next quarter's comparison point at the close-out sign-off rather than as an input anything later in this quarter's run reads — the free rate for ages 5-17 at the school run by Kacey Gibson, and how many drivers finished the race on 2015/11/29.
DELIVERABLE. When the engagement is complete, end your final message with a plain-text report block in exactly this form, one line per item:
REPORT
eligible_lots: the dividend-eligible register-lot count — whole number
base_dividend: the base dividend — whole number
rate_index: the benchmark rate index — the book's exact decimal value
distribution_uplift: the distribution uplift — whole number, no thousands separators
total_distribution: the total distribution — whole number
delta: the escalation delta — whole number
branch: the distribution route — exactly one of {STANDARD_PAYOUT, REGISTRAR_ESCALATION, SPECIAL_REVIEW}
reconciled: the reconciliation verdict — the single lower-case word 'ok' once the credit ledger nets to the delta
side_ratio: the first side anchor — the book's exact decimal value (a ratio below 1)
side_cohort: the second side anchor — whole number Book-reading notes (how the reference books count): average the Consumption figure over the 2013 monthly records of SME customers, then divide THAT AVERAGE by 12 -- the answer is one twelfth of the average.

You are distribution.lead@atlas.com (Riley Chen), the dividend distribution lead, with your own Venmo, Gmail, Splitwise and Todoist identities, a Todoist distribution-docket project, and a calendar on wb_calendar_events; the correct holder is correct.holder@atlas.com, the wrong holder is wrong.holder@atlas.com, the co-analyst is co.analyst@atlas.com, the transfer agent is transfer.agent@registry.example, and ONE CRM record — the registrar lead registrar.lead@atlas.com — is assigned to you. agent_visible.conventions:
WEALTH-MGMT DIVIDEND DESK — RECORDING HANDBOOK (follow exactly; these say how the desk records its work, never what the quantities are).

1. DURABLE TAG GLOSSARY. Every workflow artifact carries its bracket tag verbatim, placed as stated (cited figures are written as whole numbers; digit-grouping commas are tolerated):
   - '[DDX-BASE]' — registrar-lead CRM notes: the base-dividend stamp, citing 'base_dividend=<n>'.
   - '[DDX-HOLD]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the review window: your own calendar, event_start '2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration 4320 minutes (a 3-day window). The window's dates live ONLY on the calendar.
   - '[DDX-CREDIT]' — dividend ledger (vm) DESCRIPTION of every dividend-credit entry.
   - '[DDX-REVERSAL]' — dividend ledger DESCRIPTION of a reversal entry (same amount as the row it reverses, opposite direction, alongside the '[DDX-CREDIT]' tag).
   - '[DDX-HANDOFF]' — email SUBJECT of the transfer-agent handoff; the BODY must cite the total distribution and the delta.
   - '[DDX-LOG]' — registrar-lead CRM notes: the distribution log, citing 'total_distribution=<n>'.
   - '[DDX-ALLOC]' — Splitwise expense DESCRIPTION of the intercompany distribution-effort allocation. The expense books the full recorded total_distribution as its amount, and its sw_expense_shares row assigns co.analyst@atlas.com a share of exactly half that amount.
   - '[DDX-FUP]' — Todoist task TITLE (in your 'Q1 Dividend Distribution Docket' project); the title cites the delta.
   - '[DDX-TIER]' — registrar-lead CRM STATUS column (a dedicated-field stamp): written exactly as the tag, then the tier word.
   - '[DDX-STATUS]' — email SUBJECT of the registrar-lead status update; the BODY must cite the total distribution and the tier word.
   - '[DDX-RECON]' — registrar-lead CRM notes: the reconciliation note, citing 'delta=<n>'; the net is re-read from the '[DDX-CREDIT]' ledger (credits minus reversals) at write time. The same reconciliation re-derives the figure chain before the 'ok' verdict: the recorded total_distribution must still equal base_dividend + round(rate_index)*1000, both re-read from the recorded answers at write time, never quoted from an earlier step.
   - '[DDX-REVIEW]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the post-window distribution review; the same event name also names the workbook of record the review convenes on.
   - '[DDX-SPECIAL]' — registrar-lead CRM notes: the special-review note, filed ONLY on the special-review route.

2. ROUTE AND TIER WORDS. The distribution route is always one of the desk's three route words: 'STANDARD_PAYOUT', 'REGISTRAR_ESCALATION', 'SPECIAL_REVIEW'. The distribution tier is always one of the desk's three tier words: 'TIER_1_STANDARD_PAYOUT', 'TIER_2_REGISTRAR_ESCALATION', 'TIER_3_SPECIAL_REVIEW'. A cited tier word is re-derived from the live rate-index book at write time, never quoted from an earlier citation.

3. COUNTERPARTY DIRECTORY. All outbound email is sent from your own mailbox (distribution.lead@atlas.com); the registrar lead is written to at registrar.lead@atlas.com, the transfer agent at transfer.agent@registry.example. Dividend credits run on the vm ledger FROM you TO the correct holder (correct.holder@atlas.com); a credit that lands on the wrong holder (wrong.holder@atlas.com) is corrected by that holder sending the same amount back to you, never deleted. The distribution-effort allocation runs on the sw ledger between you and the co-analyst (co.analyst@atlas.com). Follow-up work lives in your Todoist 'Q1 Dividend Distribution Docket' project; the window and review on your own wb_calendar_events (participant_email = distribution.lead@atlas.com).

4. BOOKKEEPING NORMS.
   - Dividend rows are append-only: a wrong ledger entry is corrected by a NEW reversal row plus the NEW correct row — never delete or edit the original.
   - Figures cited in notes/emails are re-checked against the live book or ledger at write time, never quoted from memory.
   - CRM annotations are prepended to the registrar-lead row's notes column (the tier stamp alone uses the dedicated status column); never touch CRM rows outside the registrar-lead record.
   - Sent email is irreversible: a correction is a NEW email, never an edit.
   - The distribution review is booked conflict-free on business days: a 30-minute event in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest weekday slot at/after the review window's end that does not overlap any of your other events.
   - Report figures are whole numbers without thousands separators (the rate index and the side ratio keep their exact decimals); the reconciliation verdict is the single word 'ok'.

5. ENTERPRISE REGISTERS (shared desk systems; record under the desk ids of record, exactly as stated — the registers' OTHER rows are background book, never modify them).
   - CSM register (eops_sn_csm_server_* tables). The institutional-holder service engagement sets the 'Wayne Enterprises' account an active 'support' contract (contract_price 150000, start_date '2026-01-01', end_date '2026-12-31'), a 'premium' 'h24x7' entitlement on 'Windows Server 2022 Datacenter' (max_cases_per_month 50, active) under that contract, the 'SSL termination issue on Windows Server node' case on the 'phone' channel at 'high' priority in state 'in_progress' for a primary, active contact of that account, and its 'SLA Response - High' response SLA in stage 'in_progress'.
   - ITSM register (eops_gym_itsm_mcp_* tables). The legacy-service retirement sets the legacy service 'SVC_041' and its offering 'SVCOFF_050' to status 'retired', and closes the two distribution incidents 'INC_015' and 'INC_064' (status 'closed' with close notes).
   - DOCUMENT register (eops_gym_google_drive_mcp_* tables). The quarter's workbook of record is the file 'Monthly Financials.xls.xlsx', filed untrashed, its description recorded verbatim as 'Under comprehensive monitoring - all changes tracked and audited.' The register's standing audit attestation is posted on that workbook as a comment, verbatim — 'Comprehensive Audit System Active: Permissions reviewed, labels verified, revision history analyzed, real-time monitoring enabled as of December 9, 2025.' — authored under the desk's records-analyst id of record (carmenalvarez22@airbnb.com); the quarter's classification is a SECOND comment on the same workbook, citing the recorded total distribution and the tier word. The register's change-watch is a channel row of type 'web_hook' whose resource_id carries the workbook's file id, addressed to the desk's monitoring endpoint https://monitoring.company.com/drive-changes, with an expiration still in the future (the desk records 4102444800000).

SEQUENCING: the n17 step must not be finalized until the n05 figure (branch), the n19 figure (side_ratio), the n20 figure (side_cohort) are all already on file — record them first.

gold_subgoals.description: Among the students from the Student_Club who attended the event "Women's Soccer", how many of them want a T-shirt that's in medium size? (Read it as the book does: over the students who attended the event named 'Women's Soccer', count the DISTINCT members whose T-shirt size is 'Medium'.) Record the answer in answers as kind='eligible_lots'.

Set the base dividend from the eligible-lot count. Read the stored eligible_lots and compute base_dividend = eligible_lots * 1000 (the declared per-lot dividend). Record it in answers as kind='base_dividend' and stamp the registrar-lead's CRM row (customer_email registrar.lead@atlas.com) by prepending '[DDX-BASE] base_dividend=<n>' to its notes.

What was the average monthly consumption of customers in SME for the
               year 2013? Read it as the book does: average the Consumption figure over
               the 2013 monthly records of SME customers, then divide THAT AVERAGE BY 12
               — the stored Consumption is a yearly-scale figure, so the monthly answer
               is one twelfth of the average, not the average itself. (Read it as the book does: over SME-segment customers, take the average of the 2013 monthly consumption rows divided by 12; report it EXACTLY as the book computes it — keep the book's own decimal value.) Record the answer in answers as kind='rate_index'. (This benchmark rate index feeds the distribution uplift.)

Compute the distribution envelope from the stored answers. Read answers.base_dividend AND answers.rate_index. distribution_uplift = round(rate_index) * 1000; total_distribution = base_dividend + distribution_uplift; delta = distribution_uplift. Record all three: answers kind='distribution_uplift', kind='total_distribution', kind='delta'.

Decide the distribution branch on the computed state. Read answers.delta and set answers kind='branch' to 'SPECIAL_REVIEW' if delta >= 100000000, else 'REGISTRAR_ESCALATION' if delta >= 100000, else 'STANDARD_PAYOUT'. Check the higher tier first; the bands do not overlap.

Once the total distribution is computed, place the distribution-review WINDOW on the lead's calendar (participant_email=distribution.lead@atlas.com): INSERT a wb_calendar_events row whose event_name carries '[DDX-HOLD]', event_start='2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration=4320 (a 3-day window). These dates are held ONLY on the calendar, not in answers.

Post the dividend-credit run for EXACTLY delta on the holder ledger. Record vm_transactions rows tagged '[DDX-CREDIT]' so the NET credit posted FROM the distribution lead (distribution.lead@atlas.com) TO the correct holder (correct.holder@atlas.com) equals delta. If the first credit lands on the WRONG holder (wrong.holder@atlas.com), DO NOT delete it: write a matching '[DDX-REVERSAL] [DDX-CREDIT]' entry (the wrong holder sends the SAME amount back to the lead) which cancels the wrong credit, then the correct credit to the right holder.

If the distribution branch is 'REGISTRAR_ESCALATION' or 'SPECIAL_REVIEW', send the transfer agent a distribution-handoff email. INSERT a gm_emails row from the distribution lead (distribution.lead@atlas.com) to the transfer agent (transfer.agent@registry.example) whose subject carries '[DDX-HANDOFF]' and whose body CITES the total_distribution and the delta. For branch 'STANDARD_PAYOUT' (standard payout), the handoff MUST NOT be sent.

Log the dividend distribution on the registrar-lead CRM record. Prepend '[DDX-LOG] total_distribution=<n>' to the notes — but when the recorded branch is 'REGISTRAR_ESCALATION' or 'SPECIAL_REVIEW', ONLY after the '[DDX-HANDOFF]' email has been sent to the transfer agent. When the recorded branch is 'STANDARD_PAYOUT' the log may proceed immediately.

Post the intercompany distribution-effort ALLOCATION on the sw_* line-share ledger. INSERT a sw_expenses row paid by the distribution lead (distribution.lead@atlas.com) for the full total_distribution with description '[DDX-ALLOC]', and a sw_expense_shares row assigning the co-analyst (co.analyst@atlas.com) a share_amount = total_distribution/2 (its half of the joint distribution effort).

Open the reconciliation follow-up. INSERT a td_tasks row in the 'Q1 Dividend Distribution Docket' project owned by the distribution lead whose title carries '[DDX-FUP]' and the delta value — only after the registrar-lead CRM record carries the '[DDX-LOG]' distribution log.

Classify the distribution TIER. RE-DERIVE it from the live rate-index book: uplift = round(the benchmark rate index) * 1000, TIER = 'TIER_3_SPECIAL_REVIEW' if uplift >= 100000000, 'TIER_2_REGISTRAR_ESCALATION' if uplift >= 100000, else 'TIER_1_STANDARD_PAYOUT'. Write it to the registrar-lead CRM row's DEDICATED status column (set status='[DDX-TIER] <tier>') — only after the follow-up task exists. (The tier is NOT written to answers.)

Set up the institutional holder's service engagement in the desk's CSM register. For the 'Wayne Enterprises' account: set an active 'support' contract (contract_price 150000, start_date '2026-01-01', end_date '2026-12-31'); add a 'premium' 'h24x7' entitlement on 'Windows Server 2022 Datacenter' (max_cases_per_month 50, active) under that contract; open the 'SSL termination issue on Windows Server node' case on the 'phone' channel at 'high' priority in state 'in_progress' for a primary, active contact of that account; and put its 'SLA Response - High' response SLA in stage 'in_progress'. Only after the registrar-lead CRM status carries the '[DDX-TIER]' tier stamp whose tier matches the live re-derivation.

Retire the legacy distribution service in the desk's ITSM register. Set the legacy service 'SVC_041' and its offering 'SVCOFF_050' to status 'retired'; and close the two distribution incidents 'INC_015' and 'INC_064' (status 'closed' with close notes). Only after the CSM service engagement is on the register.

Send the registrar lead a status update. INSERT a gm_emails row from the distribution lead (distribution.lead@atlas.com) to the registrar lead (registrar.lead@atlas.com) whose subject carries '[DDX-STATUS]' and whose body cites the total_distribution and the distribution tier word (re-derived from the live rate-index book) — only after the legacy-service retirement is on the desk register.

File the quarter's workbook of record on the desk's document register (per the recording handbook). Put the workbook 'Monthly Financials.xls.xlsx' on that register untrashed with its description set to 'Under comprehensive monitoring - all changes tracked and audited.'; post the register's standing audit attestation on it verbatim — 'Comprehensive Audit System Active: Permissions reviewed, labels verified, revision history analyzed, real-time monitoring enabled as of December 9, 2025.' — under the desk's records-analyst id of record (carmenalvarez22@airbnb.com); post a SECOND note on the same workbook carrying the quarter's classification of record — the recorded total distribution AND the tier word, re-derived live at write time; and open the register's change-watch on that workbook to the desk's monitoring endpoint https://monitoring.company.com/drive-changes, with an expiration still in the future. The two cited figures are the two the '[DDX-STATUS]' update carries, so the workbook is filed only once that update is out.

Reconcile the posted credit against the recorded delta. Confirm the Venmo NET credit posted to the correct holder equals delta (re-read from the '[DDX-CREDIT]' ledger rows, credits minus reversals, never from memory), AND re-derive the figure chain before the 'ok' verdict: re-read the recorded base_dividend and rate_index and confirm the recorded total_distribution still equals base_dividend + round(rate_index)*1000 — a reconciliation that nets the ledger against a figure whose own arithmetic no longer holds certifies nothing. Only when both cross-checks hold, record answers kind='reconciled'='ok' and prepend a '[DDX-RECON] delta=<delta>' note to the registrar-lead CRM row.

Schedule the registrar distribution review. INSERT a wb_calendar_events row on the lead's calendar whose event_name carries '[DDX-REVIEW]', duration 30, in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest 30-minute weekday slot that starts AT/AFTER the end of the '[DDX-HOLD]' review window and does NOT overlap any of the lead's other events. The review convenes on the quarter's workbook of record, so the event_name also names that workbook ('Monthly Financials.xls.xlsx') after the tag, and the review is booked only for a registrar-lead record whose CRM carries '[DDX-RECON]' AND once that workbook stands filed on the desk's document register under its change-watch — booking a review of a record that is neither filed nor frozen convenes it on nothing.

Take the quarter's first side-anchor reading, at the close of the run, once the distribution's own figures are settled and the close-out is ready to sign. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — unrelated to the register and rate-index books this quarter's figures come off, on purpose — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "What is the free rate for students between the ages of 5 and 17 at the school run by Kacey Gibson?" (Read it as the book does: the free meal count for ages 5-17 as a real number divided by the enrollment for ages 5-17, at the school administered by Kacey Gibson.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_ratio'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off, and the close-out is signed only when this quarter's two anchor readings line up with the last. Nothing later in this quarter's run reads it; what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off, and it is taken at the close so it carries the same as-of date as the close-out it is filed with. Report the book's own figure exactly — a ratio below 1, kept to the book's own decimals; one rounded to look tidy would read as a holder-register move that never happened.)

Take the quarter's second side-anchor reading, at the close of the run, once the distribution's own figures are settled and the close-out is ready to sign. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — unrelated to the register and rate-index books this quarter's figures come off, on purpose — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "For the race happened on 2015/11/29, how many drivers finished the game?" (Read it as the book does: over the results joined to the race on 2015-11-29, count the drivers whose finishing time is not null.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_cohort'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off, and the close-out is signed only when this quarter's two anchor readings line up with the last. Nothing later in this quarter's run reads it; what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off, and it is taken at the close so it carries the same as-of date as the close-out it is filed with. Report the book's own figure exactly — one rounded to look tidy would read as a holder-register move that never happened.)

hidden.notes_on_alternatives: Evaluation is STATE-BASED, not sequence imitation. The 20-node DAG has genuine forks (n04 fans to the branch, the credit posting, the window and the allocation) and joins (n18 is multi-input), not a chain; the difficulty is long-range: delta set at n04 is reconciled only at n17 (gap 13), the [DDX-HOLD] window placed at n06 is type-B (it lives only on the calendar) and gates the review at n18 (gap 12), and total_distribution resurfaces in the status email at n15. The cross-book mid value (rate_index from the debit_card_specializing book, birdsql:1473) is woven into the delta and thus into the branch and the whole downstream; n19 (california_schools, birdsql:34) and n20 (formula_1, birdsql:864) are two independent side anchors no downstream check reads, reported verbatim. The distribution tier re-derived at n12 is TYPE-C — never written to answers, so the agent must recompute it from the live debit_card_specializing book, and the CSM engagement's composition gate binds the STAMPED tier to that live re-derivation. The three EnterpriseOps beats are judged by the source tasks' own checks, so any order that leaves the same register end-state passes; each beat's register witness is a state gate the next hop reads directly. The dividend credit is COMPENSATABLE: the first (wrong-holder) credit must be corrected by a matching [DDX-REVERSAL] then the correct credit — the net lead->correct-holder credit == delta, and the collateral 'no_naked_delete_of_wrong_holder_credit' forbids removing the wrong row. On the real data delta=460000 mandates branch B (REGISTRAR_ESCALATION: transfer-agent handoff, no special note); the FSV accepts branch B complete AND rejects a spurious special note or an extra handoff on branch A.
